section.p: The keeper wrote every passing ship into a ledger bound in sailcloth. By the third winter the ledger held more names than the village did, and the keeper began to wonder which of them would ever come back.
On calm nights he read the entries aloud to the lamp, as if the light might carry them further than his voice.
Under the stairs was a tin box of letters addressed to ships rather than people. None had stamps. Each one began the same way: if this reaches you before the fog does.
The keeper never posted them. He said a letter kept was a promise still open.
